State the theorem you are using
Set up the equation and solve
method_card.title: Circle Theorems
method_card.content:
Angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference (subtended by the same arc).

Angle in a semicircle is \(90°\). Angles in the same segment are equal. Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to \(180°\).

Tangent-radius: A tangent meets the radius at \(90°\). Two tangents from an external point are equal in length. Alternate segment theorem: The angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment.
method_card.example:
Angle at centre = 110°. Find the angle at circumference.

Angle at circumference = \(110 \div 2 = 55°\) (angle at centre is twice angle at circumference).

gold.display: O is the centre. A, B, C on circle. Angle OAB = \(25°\). Find angle ACB.

misconceptions.message: OA = OB (radii), so triangle OAB is isosceles. OBA = 25°. AOB = 180−50 = 130°. ACB = 130 ÷ 2 = 65°.

gold.display: A, B, C, D lie on a circle. Angle ABC = \(3x + 10\), angle ADC = \(2x + 20\). Find angle ABC.
PT is a tangent at T. A, T, B on circle. Angle PTA = \(70°\). Angle ATB = \(x\). AB is a chord where angle in alternate segment to PTA = angle ABT. Find angle ABT.

misconceptions.message: By the alternate segment theorem, angle ABT = angle PTA = 70°.

gold.display: A, B, C, D are on a circle. AB is a diameter. Angle CAB = \(28°\). Find angle ADB.

misconceptions.message: ACB = 90° (angle in semicircle). In triangle ACB: ABC = 180−90−28 = 62°. ADB = ABC = 62° (same segment).

gold.display: O is the centre. A, B on circle. Angle OAB = \(35°\). C is on the minor arc. Find the obtuse angle ACB.

misconceptions.message: OAB isosceles: OBA=35. AOB=180-70=110. Reflex AOB=250. C on minor arc: ACB = 250/2 = 125.

bronze.display: The angle at the centre of a circle is \(124°\). Find the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc.

misconceptions.message: The angle at the circumference is HALF the angle at the centre: 124 ÷ 2 = 62°.

bronze.display: The angle at the circumference is \(48°\). Find the angle at the centre.

misconceptions.message: The angle at the centre is TWICE the angle at circumference: 48 × 2 = 96°.

bronze.display: AB is a diameter. C is on the circumference. Find angle ACB.

misconceptions.message: Angle in a semicircle is always 90°.

bronze.display: In a cyclic quadrilateral, one angle is \(72°\). Find the opposite angle.

misconceptions.message: Opposite angles in a cyclic quad sum to 180°: 180 − 72 = 108°.

bronze.display: Two angles in the same segment are \(x\) and \(35°\). Find \(x\).

misconceptions.message: Angles in the same segment are equal. x = 35°.

bronze.display: A tangent meets a radius at point P. The angle between them is:

misconceptions.message: A tangent always meets the radius at 90°.

bronze.display: The angle at the centre is \(150°\). Find the angle at the circumference.

misconceptions.message: Circumference angle = centre angle ÷ 2 = 150 ÷ 2 = 75°.

bronze.display: Angle ACB = 90° (C on circle, AB is diameter). If angle BAC = 32°, find angle ABC.

misconceptions.message: Triangle angles sum to 180°: 90 + 32 + ABC = 180 → ABC = 58°.

silver.display: A cyclic quadrilateral has angles \(3x\), \(2x + 10\), \(x + 40\) and \(100°\). The angles \(3x\) and \(x + 40\) are opposite. Find \(x\).

misconceptions.message: Opposite angles sum to 180°: 3x + x + 40 = 180 → 4x = 140 → x = 35.

silver.display: The angle between a tangent and a chord at the point of contact is \(64°\). Find the angle in the alternate segment.

misconceptions.message: Alternate segment theorem: the angle equals the angle in the alternate segment = 64°.

silver.display: O is the centre. Angle AOB = \(x + 50\). Angle ACB = \(x\) (C on circumference, same side as major arc). Find \(x\).

misconceptions.message: Centre = 2 × circumference: x + 50 = 2x → x = 50°.

silver.display: Two tangents from an external point T touch the circle at A and B. TA = 12 cm. Find TB.

misconceptions.message: Two tangents from the same external point are equal in length. TB = 12 cm.

silver.display: O is the centre of the circle. Angle BOC = \(140°\). Find the reflex angle BOC.

misconceptions.message: Reflex angle = 360 − 140 = 220°.

silver.display: The angle between a tangent at A and chord AB is \(52°\). O is the centre. Find angle AOB.

misconceptions.message: Alternate segment: angle in alternate segment = 52°. Angle at centre = 2 × 52 = 104°.

silver.display: Points A, B, C lie on a circle. Angle BAC = \(40°\) and angle BCA = \(55°\). Find angle ABC.

misconceptions.message: Angles in a triangle: 40 + 55 + ABC = 180 → ABC = 85°.

steps.label: Opposite angles sum to 180°
steps.content:
85 + 95 = 180 ✓. Also x + 2x = 180 (they're the other pair, but check which are opposite).

Actually: 85° is opposite 95°: 85+95=180 ✓. x is opposite 2x: x + 2x = 180.

worked_examples.question: A cyclic quadrilateral has angles 85°, x, 95° and 2x. Find x.

steps.label: Alternate segment theorem
steps.content: The angle between the tangent and chord = the angle in the alternate segment.

worked_examples.question: A tangent and a radius meet at point P on the circle. The angle between the tangent and a chord PQ is 55°. Find the angle in the alternate segment.
